text:
bob_support: Heads up — ACME (acme-prod) opened a ticket: /v1/fncall is returning 500s and the payload parser is failing with 'invalid function args'. They see retries and a big billing spike.

bob_support: Sample error from our runtime: 
```
ERROR: fncall_handler: invalid args: key 'order_ids' expected Array<Integer> but got \"[\"123\",\"456\"]\" (string)
stack: runtime.parser.parse_args -> runtime.handler.invoke
```

bob_support: They say they didn't change client code; started failing ~2026-11-02T14:02Z. Also seeing intermittent 401s before the 500s.

dylan_eng: Can we get the raw request body they sent? Also which SDK version?

bob_support: Pasting sanitized request (customer masked ids): 
```
POST /v1/fncall
Headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "gpt-open-1",
  "mode": "json",
  "function": "create_shipment",
  "args": "{\"order_ids\": \"[\\\"123\\\",\\\"456\\\"]\", \"warehouse\": \"east-1\" }"
}
```

bob_support: SDK reported: "sdk-js@2.4.1" in their app metadata.

dylan_eng: That looks like double-encoded args — args should be an object when json mode is used, not a stringified JSON. Did SDK 2.4.1 change coercion behavior?

alice.dev: We shipped a patch in sdk-js 2.4.1 that tightened backwards-compat coercion for args to avoid ambiguous types. It prevents silently converting stringified JSON into objects — intended but will break clients that relied on coercion.

clara_sre: Impact: these requests hit our strict-json path, we attempt schema validation -> error -> runtime returns 400 normally, but because the function handler layer has a bug with a null pointer on validation failure for certain tool plugins it escalates to 500 and triggers automatic retries. We're seeing retry storms for some tenants.

bob_support: ACME observed 500s (not 400) and their client retried with exponential backoff — billing shows repeated token usage.

billing_bot: Detected >3x baseline token usage for tenant acme-prod between 2026-11-02T14:00Z and 14:45Z. Temporarily flagged for review. Possible cause: retries from client + streaming reattempts.

dylan_eng: Repro plan — we should reproduce in staging with sdk-js@2.4.1 and previous 2.3.x. Steps: 1) Send fncall with args as stringified JSON 2) Observe validation behavior 3) Confirm whether error code is 400 vs 500 and whether retries are triggered.

alice.dev: I'll reproduce locally. Quick mitigation: enable a per-tenant coercion compatibility toggle that accepts stringified args for now and return 400 (not 500) when invalid. Also patch the function-handler NPE.

clara_sre: For production immediate mitigation I suggest: 1) rate-limit retries per API key to slow down cost growth, 2) set a temporary fallback to lenient-parse model variant in region us-east-1 for acme-prod, 3) disable automatic heavy retries in the routing layer for 'json' mode failures.

bob_support: ACME also mentioned they saw some 401s earlier in the window. Auth logs show a couple of short-lived token validations failing (introspect service 503) right before the parser errors. Could be unrelated cascade.

dylan_eng: Noted. We'll check auth service traces. If auth intermittency caused client to re-auth and resend payloads, that could amplify the retry storm.

alice.dev: Repro result: sdk-js@2.3.5 accepts the stringified args and our runtime coerces -> returns 200 (old behavior). sdk-js@2.4.1 sends the same payload and our strict-json path rejects -> produces 500 because of the validation plugin NPE. I have a PR ready to catch validation errors and return 400: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/4123 (WIP).

dylan_eng: Good. Also add a check to prevent retries on 4xx. Our client-side guidance should be: do not retry on 400/422 for fncall. We'll push an advisory to docs and send customer note.

bob_support: Customer impact summary for ACME: repeated failed fncalls (500) for ~15m, 3x token usage spike, some failed orders. They requested either a rollback to permissive parsing or an immediate patch.

clara_sre: Action items: 
- alice.dev: hotfix to return 400 on schema validation and patch NPE (ETA 2h).
- dylan_eng: reproduce with auth intermittency and confirm cascade (ETA 1h).
- deploy-bot: prepare canary for hotfix to acme-prod traffic only.
- billing_bot: create temporary billing hold and manual review alert for acme-prod.

deploy-bot: Canary pipeline queued: runtime-hotfix-canary -> will deploy to 5% acme-prod traffic after alice.dev + test signoff.

billing_bot: Placed tenant acme-prod on manual billing review; flagged anomalies and prevented automated overages for now.

bob_support: I'll send ACME the interim workaround: add a small client patch to ensure args is JSON (not string) or pin SDK to 2.3.x. Also gave them ETA ~2-3 hours.

alice.dev: Hotfix PR created and tests added for stringified-args -> returns 400 and no retry. Link: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/4123. Deploying to staging now.

dylan_eng: Found auth trace: token service had a 503 window caused by DB failover 2026-11-02T13:58Z. That likely caused some client replays. I filed infra incident INC-2026-231.

bob_support: ACME replied: "Thanks — rolling pin to 2.3.x now, will monitor. Please confirm when fix is live."

clara_sre: I'll watch SLOs and billing dashboard. If we still see >2x usage after canary, we'll throttle.

alice.dev: Deployed hotfix to canary for acme-prod. Tests pass. Waiting 10m for telemetry.

bob_support: ACME confirmed partial recovery after pin. They've downgraded SDK and are seeing fewer 500s. :thumbsup:

clara_sre: Telemetry: error rate for fncall on acme-prod dropped from 12% -> 1.8% after canary. Token usage trending down.

bob_support: Closing loop with customer and documenting root cause: SDK coercion change + runtime validation NPE + auth intermittency = amplified retry/billing spike. Will follow up with a changelog note and recommended pin/upgrade guidance.

alice.dev: Follow-up: we'll add a compatibility flag and a changelog entry in sdk-js. Also adding a postmortem doc.

bob_support: Thanks all.
